item.title: Australia’s endangered palm cockatoos get artificial nests; first chick fledges in world-first
item.description: A palm cockatoo chick has recently fledged from an artificial hollow in the Cape York Peninsula, marking a positive step for conservationists. They installed 29 artificial nesting hollows to combat the lack of natural breeding sites. This first successful breeding event is a pivotal achievement in palm cockatoo conservation. Ongoing monitoring will assess how well these new hollows can facilitate nesting and chick growth for this endangered species. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: More than a million mice used in Australian research annually, ‘overdue’ study finds
item.description: Advocates say having national data about numbers of rats and mice used in research can help boost public trust in science Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast More than a million mice and nearly 47,000 rats are used in scientific research in Australia annually, according to the first ever nationwide count. Dr Malcolm France, a veterinarian who compiled the data, described the count, released today, as “an overdue first step” towards publishing national statistics for all animals used in research, including fish, rabbits, birds and monkeys. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - Environment.

item.title: Australian politicians say they are paying thousands for their own security upgrades amid rising threats
item.description: Home and office safety a common concern in Australian federal police and Asio safety briefings with politicians following alleged attack on MP Helen Haines Get our new political email , free app or daily news podcast Security agencies will review safety precautions for MPs’ homes and offices after numerous federal politicians told police and Asio in safety briefings that they were worried about widening threats after the alleged attack on Helen Haines. The Labor government and politicians across the parliament are still considering how they will respond when they return to Canberra next week… Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Majority of Australians who report penicillin allergy not truly allergic
item.description: Peak body for immunologists changes guidelines as evidence shows up to 90% of those reporting allergy don’t have one Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast The majority of Australians who report a penicillin allergy are not truly allergic, prompting the peak body for immunologists to change its guidelines in a bid to reduce hospitals stays and tackle antimicrobial resistance. Penicillin, one of the most commonly prescribed antibiotics in Australia, was thought to cause allergies in 10% of Australians, or about 2.8 million people. Continue reading... Fuente: The Guardian - World.

item.title: Australia releases 50 critically endangered smoky mice into forest after decades of absence
item.description: Australia has successfully reintroduced almost 50 critically endangered smoky mice into South East Forest National Park. This reintroduction represents a significant step towards restoring the region’s ecosystem and native mammal populations. Various species, including the long-footed potoroo and eastern quoll, are also planned for reintroduction. The effort is part of a broader initiative by the NSW Government and conservationists. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Margot Robbie’s renovated Hollywood bungalow sold for $1.2 million
item.description: In February 2018, Margot Robbie bought a charming 945-square-foot bungalow in Hollywood Heights for $950,000. After giving it a stylish makeover, she rented it out at various rates. She eventually sold the property in 2021 for around $1.2 million, marking a profitable investment. This venture underscores the appeal of smaller homes in attractive neighborhoods, complementing her extensive property collection across Los Angeles and Australia. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
